messages:
maria: Heads up — saw GPU nodes filling with non-GPU pods this morning, causing fragmentation and a surprise scale-up of the GPU pool. Cost spike ~18% for the cluster. Anyone else seeing this? :grimacing:

maria: quick snapshot:
```
$ kubectl get nodes -l nodepool=gpu-us-east-1a -o wide
NAME            STATUS   ROLES    AGE   VERSION   TAINTS
gpu-node-12     Ready    <none>   5d    v1.26.4   gpu=true:PreferNoSchedule
gpu-node-13     Ready    <none>   3d    v1.26.4   gpu=true:PreferNoSchedule
```
And some pods without GPU requests on those nodes:
```
$ kubectl get pods -o=custom-columns=NAME,NODE,CPU,GPUS
ci-runner-7     gpu-node-12 100m  0
api-proxy-19    gpu-node-13 50m   0
```
I think the ``PreferNoSchedule`` taint + a permissive toleration in our CI templates combined to push CPU work onto GPUs.

jon: ugh. do we have an admission webhook that adds tolerations? or did someone add a blanket toleration in deploy templates?

maria: looks like the CI image runner has a toleration we added months ago to avoid evictions during drain:
```
 tolerations:
 - operator: Exists
```
That one toleration will tolerate any taint key on the node (operator: Exists) — so it happily lands on GPU nodes despite not needing a GPU.

li: That explains it. PreferNoSchedule is a soft hint so kube-scheduler will still put pods there if nothing else blocks them. Combined with operator: Exists toleration it's a free pass.

infra-bot: autoscaler: ScaleUp request for nodepool gpu-us-east-1a (+2) triggered at 2026-03-12T08:04:31Z due to pending GPU-bound workloads.

sam: Do we know which workloads actually needed GPUs and were preempted or delayed?

maria: Yes — two training jobs were pending for ~12m; once the autoscaler added nodes they scheduled, but→ cost + extra idle time while we drained the CPU-only pods.

jon: Proposed fixes:
- tighten tolerations: replace `operator: Exists` with explicit key/value (e.g., `key: run-ci, operator: Equal, value: true`), only applied to pods that should tolerate GPU taints
- change node taint to `NoSchedule` for stricter isolation for prod GPU pools, and `PreferNoSchedule` for dev/test pools
- add required nodeAffinity for GPU workloads (requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution) to ensure they only schedule on gpu nodes
- add a mutating webhook to inject proper tolerations instead of blanket Exists

li: Also watch cluster-autoscaler behavior: if pods that prefer GPUs have NO gpu resource requests, autoscaler will scale non-gpu pools. For actual GPU jobs we should ensure they request `nvidia.com/gpu: 1`.

maria: Agreed. Steps I'm pushing now:
1) patch CI runner chart to remove `operator: Exists` toleration and add specific toleration key `ci-runner=true` (rollback safe)
2) create RFC to change prod GPU nodepool taint to `NoSchedule` (we'll need a migration plan)
3) add alert on "GPU node CPU utilization > 70% && free GPUs == 0" so we detect CPU-only pods crowding GPU nodes

sam: small nit — we should also add a lint rule in our infra-linter to flag `tolerations.operator: Exists` in manifests. Too many historical footguns.

jon: I'll own the autoscaler watch item and run a quick query to verify if any pending pods lack `nvidia.com/gpu` requests. Will post results in ~15m.

maria: thanks. If we decide to flip to `NoSchedule` for prod, plan: cordon + drain CPU-only pods from GPU nodes over a day, schedule replacement nodes, and rolling reboot. Need SRE signoff.

li: +1 to gating changes behind a rollout and a canary. We can also update the console docs so app teams know which key/value tolerations are allowed.

infra-bot: NOTE: created issue #INFRA-847 (tighten-gpu-tolerations) and added to sprint backlog.

maria: ok closing loop for now — action items assigned. Thanks all :thumbsup:
